meeting_header: Date: 2026-05-11 | Time: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 54 min | Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jordan Li (Redwood SE), Olivia Gomez (Crestline), Samir Khan (Crestline), Aisha Brown (Crestline)
summary: Redwood AE/SE walked Crestline through the Console usage analytics, per-route dashboards and detailed cost breakdown. Customer cares about per-route cost visibility, routing policies for peak shopping hours, and SOC 2/network diagrams. Agreed to pilot cart-recommendation route with sample traffic and run benchmarks week of May 24.
transcript: 00:00 Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm Maya from Redwood. we'll do a quick console walkthrough focused on usage analytics and cost breakdown. 00:07 Olivia: hi thanks, excited — we only have about 50 minutes so please jump to the cost parts early. 00:12 Jordan: sure, i'll share my screen now, give me one sec, um fyi audio might be a bit laggy. 00:28 Jordan: (screen) so this is the Redwood Console landing page, top-left you can toggle environment hosted vs dedicated, right away you can see token spend, requests, error rate time series. 00:45 Samir: quick q — can you break that down by route? we have like 12 endpoints and only 2 drive 80% of cost. 00:52 Jordan: yep that's the per-route dashboard, click "Routes" on the nav, it lists routes with QPS, p95 latency, and cost per 1k tokens. 01:10 Jordan: note that cost calc here includes model variant, quantization profile and batching config — so you can see where cheapest costs per token come from. 01:24 Aisha: sorry can you explain quantization profile? CFO voice: trying to understand financial impact. 01:31 Jordan: yeah so quantization profile is the model/precision combo — e.g., int8 vs fp16 — which affects price and sometimes latency; console will recommend a profile per route based on latency SLOs and quality tolerance. 01:48 Olivia: do you surface quality regressions when you switch profiles? we can't have recommendation quality degrade cart recs. 01:55 Jordan: good point — Optimize ties to our evals; if quality drops on your saved prompt set we'll flag it and add a regression alert. 02:08 Maya: also, you can pin a route to a model version or set a canary rollout across models. that helps for gradual migration. 02:17 Samir: about the cost numbers — what's included? gpu runtime, payload size, anything else? 02:22 Jordan: it's token units (inference tokens), plus a per-request overhead we model for RPC and network egress; for Dedicated we show committed capacity discounts applied. 02:36 Samir: hmm, how accurate is the per-route estimate vs actual billing? we need to reconcile in our finance system. 02:42 Maya: our numbers match invoiced units within 2-4% in historical customers; we also export per-token billing CSVs and have an API endpoint to fetch raw usage for reconciliation. 02:56 Aisha: can we get a sample CSV? we'll need line-items per route and model to map to our chargeback. 03:02 Maya: yes — action: i will send an example export after the call. 03:07 Jordan: back to console, you can drill into a route and see top prompts / prompt length distribution, which feeds into estimated token spend. 03:18 Jordan: here's an example for a cart-recommendation route — avg request 120 tokens, 20% long tail over 512 tokens which spikes cost; console highlights that and suggests prefix caching or adjusting max_tokens. 03:33 Olivia: prefix caching — can you explain. 03:36 Jordan: sure — for routes with repeated context we cache KV prefix which avoids re-computation and reduces per-token work; console suggests which prefixes to cache and estimated savings. 03:49 Samir: that sounds useful, what about batching? during promo hours we get sudden bursts. 03:55 Jordan: batching helps throughput but adds latency; console simulates batching effects given your latency SLO and recommends the batch size. you can also set autoscale/burst policies on Dedicated to handle promo spikes. 04:12 Maya: we support routing policies too — e.g., route X goes to hosted for 99% of traffic and Dedicated for premium customers or vice versa. 04:21 Olivia: security — we need SOC 2 and network diagrams for our procurement. do you provide SOC2 and VPC architecture? 04:28 Maya: yes, we have SOC 2 Type II; i'll share the report and a network diagram showing private control plane for Redwood Private and VPC peering details. 04:39 Aisha: encryption at rest / KMS options? 04:43 Jordan: customer-managed KMS supported for Private and Dedicated; hosted uses Redwood KMS with customer-managed keys for enterprise plans. 04:52 Samir: latency SLOs for Dedicated? we target p95 < 300ms for our cart route right now. 04:58 Jordan: Dedicated with optimized kernels typically gets sub-200ms for similar setups — we'll include similar benchmark numbers and suggest config to hit p95 targets. 05:12 Olivia: do you have any customers in retail who've run similar pilots? case studies? 05:18 Maya: yes — we worked with Nova Commerce on cart recs; we can share anonymized benchmarks and a short case deck. 05:25 Aisha: pricing — high level numbers please, ballpark. 05:29 Maya: ballpark hosted inference price per 1k tokens is X for smaller models, Y for advanced; i will send a tailored quote for your 10M tokens/month mix. Dedicated pricing is committed capacity plus per-token overage adjustments — i'll include both scenarios. 05:48 Samir: for the pilot we just want a week of benchmarks with our sample traffic — low risk. 05:53 Jordan: good, we'll need a sample of 7 days of traffic and success metrics (CTR, AOV lift target). we'll run a head-to-head with your current provider and share p95, throughput, and cost per prediction. 06:07 Maya: recap: send pricing + SOC2 + network diagram; Jordan to send benchmark harness + sample script; crestline to provide traffic and KPIs. plan pilot week of May 24. 06:20 Olivia: that works, thanks. 06:23 Aisha: thanks, appreciate the clear cost breakdown. 06:25 Maya: thanks all, i'll follow up with an email and the next steps. 06:28 Jordan: thanks everyone, bye. 06:30 (call ends)
notes: Transcript contains small transcription errors and typical speech patterns; action items agreed.
